skill.name: tool-design

skill.summary: Guides teams in designing clear, reliable tools for AI agents.

content.value_statement: Agent tools often fail when names, parameters, outputs, and errors are ambiguous. This skill provides design patterns for clearer tool contracts, better recovery, and stronger agent selection.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to write clear tool descriptions with usage triggers, inputs, returns, and errors.
Provides guidance for consolidating related tools to reduce agent selection ambiguity.
Describes MCP naming practices using fully qualified tool names.
Shows examples of concise and detailed response formats for token-aware tool outputs.
Includes evaluation criteria for testing clarity, completeness, recoverability, efficiency, and consistency.
limitations: Does not implement production-ready tools or connectors.
Does not validate tool schemas against a live framework.
Does not benchmark model performance automatically.
Examples are instructional and must be adapted before deployment.

use_cases.title: Create a new agent tool
use_cases.description: Define names, parameters, outputs, and error responses before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve a confusing tool set
use_cases.description: Find overlapping tools, vague descriptions, and inconsistent parameter names.

use_cases.title: Review MCP tool conventions
use_cases.description: Standardize fully qualified tool names and selection guidance across servers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic tool description
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a clear description for a tool named [tool name]. Include when to use it, required inputs, return format, and common errors.

prompt_templates.title: Compare tool boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review these tools for overlap: [tool list]. Recommend which tools to consolidate, keep separate, or rename.

prompt_templates.title: Design recovery-focused errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design error responses for [tool workflow]. Include specific failure codes, clear messages, retry guidance, and corrected input examples.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a full tool collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate this tool collection against clarity, completeness, recoverability, efficiency, and consistency. Provide prioritized changes with rationale.

output_examples.input: Review a customer lookup tool with vague parameters and no error details.
output_examples.output: The review identifies unclear parameter names, missing usage triggers, and weak recovery guidance. It recommends a specific customer identifier format, concise and detailed output modes, and actionable validation errors.

output_examples.input: Decide whether three scheduling tools should be consolidated.
output_examples.output: The assessment explains that listing attendees, checking availability, and creating an event belong to one scheduling workflow. It recommends one comprehensive scheduling tool with explicit boundaries.

output_examples.input: Standardize MCP tool references across a project.
output_examples.output: The result recommends fully qualified tool names, consistent namespace prefixes, and examples that show when each server-specific tool should be selected.

best_practices: Document what each tool does, when to use it, what inputs it accepts, and what it returns.
Use consistent naming for similar parameters, outputs, and error fields across all tools.
Test tool descriptions with realistic agent requests and revise based on observed failures.
anti_patterns: Do not create many overlapping tools when one clear workflow tool would reduce ambiguity.
Do not use vague tool names or parameter names that force agents to guess intent.
Do not return generic errors that omit the cause, expected format, or recovery step.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps teams design tools that AI agents can choose and use reliably.

faq.question: Does this skill create tool code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, examples, and review criteria for tool interfaces.

faq.question: Can it help with MCP tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for fully qualified MCP tool names and clear server context.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, platform engineers, and AI teams building tools for agent workflows should use it.

faq.question: Does it include testing advice?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends evaluating tools for clarity, completeness, recoverability, efficiency, and consistency.

faq.question: Is it specific to one AI assistant?
faq.answer: No. The guidance is useful for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other agent systems.
